title: Tracking GWACs and IDIQs Beyond SAM.gov (2026 Guide)
summary: SEWP VI, OASIS+, and Polaris are moving at once. Winners track every vehicle, not just one.
body_text: Quick answer: A GWAC is a pre-competed, multiple-award IDIQ restricted to IT products and services, sponsored government-wide by GSA, NASA, or NIH. An IDIQ is the broader contract type underneath it: any vehicle, GWAC or otherwise, that lets an agency place task orders against a pre-set ceiling instead of running a new procurement. If you're reading this, that part isn't news. The part that actually determines pipeline is structural: which of the 30+ active multiple-award vehicles your task orders are moving through right now, and whether your team sees them the moment they post. ‍ That's the problem worth talking about in 2026, because the vehicle landscape underneath most federal IT and services spend is shifting on multiple fronts at once. ‍ The vehicle landscape isn't static right now If your coverage strategy is built around the vehicles you qualified for two or three years ago, it's already out of date. A few things happening in parallel: ‍ SEWP VI is finally moving. NASA announced awards on June 22, 2026, naming 1,490 vendors across 2,115 awards, after the original April 30 target slipped under a wave of pre-award protests. SEWP VI adds two new standalone categories, Enterprise Solutions and IT Services, expanding well past the hardware-and-software scope SEWP V was known for. Ordering is expected to open around November 1, 2026, with SEWP V extended through January 2027 to bridge the transition and a 10-year ordering window running through October 2036. Teams holding SEWP V positions need a plan for the overlap window, not just a plan for day one of SEWP VI. ‍ OASIS+ moved to a rolling on-ramp model. Phase II went live January 12, 2026, replacing the old windowed on-ramp cycle with continuous acceptance of proposals. More than 1,300 small businesses are already on the $60B services vehicle, and unlike a traditional GWAC refresh, there's no fixed window to wait for or miss. ‍ Polaris is still phasing in, without a published cadence. GSA issued notice to proceed for 17 additional SDVOSB Phase II awardees on July 7, 2026, but hasn't published a recurring on-ramp schedule the way OASIS+ now has. That makes Polaris a vehicle to monitor opportunistically rather than plan around a known date. ‍ Layer that on top of the vehicles that aren't moving, ITES-4H, Alliant, CIO-SP3, and the dozens of agency-specific IDIQs that never make GWAC headlines, and the coverage question gets a lot harder than "are we on the right vehicle." ‍ The real gap: coverage, not classification For a team that already understands multiple-award IDIQs, on-ramps, and task order competition, the operational risk isn't misunderstanding a GWAC. It's that 80-90% of solicitations never touch SAM.gov at all. They post inside agency ordering portals and vehicle-specific systems, SEWP's own portal, GSA eBuy for OASIS+ and Alliant, service branch systems for ITES-4H, and dozens more, each with its own login, its own cadence, and its own notification quirks. ‍ At small scale, a BD rep can bookmark the three or four portals that matter and check them by hand. At the scale a mature GovCon sales org actually operates, across primes, OEM channel partners, and a growing vehicle list, that manual approach breaks. Teams using Govly routinely surface 500+ additional solicitations in a single search that a SAM.gov-only tool would never have shown them, and that gap only widens as more vehicles (OASIS+'s rolling model, SEWP VI's expanded categories) come online. ‍ The cost isn't abstract. It's a task order your team never saw until a competitor had already engaged the contracting officer, or a SEWP VI opportunity missed during the SEWP V/VI overlap because nobody was watching both systems at once. ‍ What mature capture teams actually need from vehicle tracking Understanding a vehicle isn't the bottleneck for teams already selling into the federal market. Operationalizing coverage across a growing, shifting set of vehicles is. That's the specific gap Govly is built to close: ‍ ‍ Real-time visibility across 30+ vehicles. Govly tracks contract vehicles including ITES-4H, SEWP, Alliant, and CIO-SP3, and updates as solicitations post, not on a weekly or monthly refresh. For vehicles moving as fast as OASIS+'s rolling on-ramp, or the SEWP V-to-VI transition window, that speed determines whether your team engages early or finds out from a competitor. ‍ One feed instead of a dozen portals. Consolidating agency ordering systems and vehicle portals into a single view means capture and BD leads aren't manually reconciling a spreadsheet against five different logins to know what's actually live. ‍ Collaboration built for teaming, not just tracking. Large IDIQ and GWAC task orders routinely involve primes, subs, and channel partners working the same opportunity. Govly lets teams share opportunities and coordinate capture without requiring every partner to hold a paid seat, replacing the "bring-your-own-contract-spreadsheet" workaround most teaming arrangements default to. ‍ Award data for positioning, not just pipeline. Seeing who won past task orders on a vehicle, and at what value, is what turns "we're on SEWP VI" into an actual go-to-market plan for where to compete. ‍ For teams already fluent in this market, that combination, full-vehicle coverage, real-time alerts, and teaming infrastructure, is what separates a vehicle award from an actual revenue outcome. ‍ FAQ ‍ How does OASIS+'s rolling on-ramp change capture planning compared to a traditional GWAC on-ramp? Traditional GWAC on-ramps open on a fixed schedule and close after a defined window, so capture teams plan around a known date. OASIS+ Phase II accepts proposals continuously, which removes the "wait for the window" dynamic but also removes the forcing function of a deadline. Teams need an ongoing readiness posture rather than a one-time push. ‍ ‍ What should teams with SEWP V positions do during the SEWP VI transition? With SEWP V extended through January 2027 and SEWP VI ordering expected to open around November 1, 2026, there's an overlap window where both vehicles are active. Task orders can post to either system during that period, so coverage needs to span both rather than assuming activity moves cleanly from one to the other on a single cutover date. ‍ ‍ Is Polaris worth tracking if there's no published on-ramp schedule? Yes, but differently than OASIS+ or SEWP. Without a recurring on-ramp cadence, Polaris activity (like the July 2026 SDVOSB Phase II notice to proceed) tends to surface as one-off GSA announcements rather than a plannable cycle, which makes real-time monitoring more valuable, not less. ‍ ‍ How many contract vehicles does a typical federal BD team actually need to track? It depends on the vertical, but most IT-focused sellers are competing across somewhere between 10 and 30 active vehicles once agency-specific IDIQs are included alongside the major GWACs. Govly tracks 30+ of them in one feed. ‍ ‍ Does a tool like Govly replace the need to hold a position on a vehicle? No. You still need to win a spot on the relevant IDIQs and GWACs to be eligible for task orders. What changes is visibility: once you're on the vehicle, real-time tracking determines whether you see (and can act on) task orders as they post, versus finding out after a competitor already has. ‍ Managing coverage across SEWP VI, OASIS+, Polaris, and 30+ other vehicles in one place. title: Digitization, data and AI are critical drivers for transport and logistics organizations to advance their priorities
summary: The impetus to accelerate digitization is growing in the transport and logistics industry. In light of today’s digital expectations, becoming data-driven is vital. However, the 2023 Voice of Our Clients (VOC) research reveals that organizational readiness and access to high-quality data and IT talent remain hurdles that transport and logistics companies must strive to overcome.
body_text: The impetus to accelerate digitization is growing in the transport and logistics industry. In light of today’s digital expectations, becoming data-driven is vital. However, the 2023 Voice of Our Clients (VOC) research reveals that organizational readiness and access to high-quality data and IT talent remain hurdles that transport and logistics companies must strive to overcome. This year, CGI leaders conducted 1,764 interviews across 21 industries, including 72 in transport and logistics. In this blog, I reflect on the most striking results from those conversations with transport and logistics executives, 57% of whom are part of the C-suite. More and more organizations derive value from digitization The good news is that the percentage of companies producing expected results from their digitization strategy has risen again, from 25% last year to 30% this year. This steady increase indicates that transport and logistics executives are embedding digitization strategies and technologies into their organizations as a critical step to navigating new market realities, including a growing number of large platform players for supply chain visibility or demand-supply matching, a rise in “as-a-service” models such as MaaS (mobility-as-a-service), ongoing global trade and supply chain disruptions and an urgent need to address climate change. Furthermore, the percentage of executives extending their digital strategy to include their ecosystem partners (customers/suppliers/competitors) continues to rise—from 39% in 2022 to 41% this year. Digitization and sustainability go hand-in-hand. This year, 75% of executives cite sustainability as highly core to creating future value, second only to the manufacturing sector (82%). In our conversations with European transport and logistics executives, they view the new Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) as a key driver to speed up digitization underpinned by a strong data-driven foundation. Data is foundational for success In most VOC conversations with transport and logistics executives, data's importance, role and uses is a central theme. While some organizations have begun their journey to become data-driven, there is still a lot of ground to cover. For instance, only 15% of executives rate their current level of maturity for using data and digitization as high. We see this small group as those that have transitioned to a data-driven enterprise. However, other organizations—including some that report achieving expected results from their digitization strategy—indicate that they need to take significant steps to improve data strategies. Of the planned improvements, data quality (85%) and data governance and management (82%) are cited as the top priorities to implement in the next 3 years. Executives view these priorities as the basic requirements to successfully transform into a data-driven organization. Automation and digital twins will accelerate once these foundational elements are in place. In a recent white paper on data sharing , my colleague Natasja van der Keijl and I discussed these prerequisites that this year's VOC findings underscore once again. Artificial intelligence is on the radar Closely related to data is a growing focus on artificial intelligence (AI). Half of the executives we interviewed indicate they are investigating how to use AI in their business process, a big jump from 31% last year. That said, only 3% say they are in the "done" stage of AI implementation—a tiny increase from 2% last year. In 2019, I authored a blog (in Dutch) that summarized the importance for transport and logistics organizations to embrace advanced analytics (focusing more on predictive and prescriptive), integrating learning capacity within the planning, and how organizations can achieve this. Lack of business-IT alignment intensifies The number of executives indicating a lack of business-IT alignment is increasing. This includes aspects such as how well business and IT understand each other and IT's ability to identify the right solutions for business issues. Only 37% say their business and IT operations are highly aligned (a score of 8 or higher on a scale of 1-10), 10 percentage points lower than 2022. A notable 43% say their business and IT teams are not aligned (a score of 1-2). This finding is not entirely surprising, as digital leaders (those producing expected results from their digital strategies) are far ahead in this area (71% of digital leaders score themselves 8 or higher) compared to digital aspirants (those building or launching their digital strategies). In addition to achieving closer alignment between business and IT operations, digital leaders also modernize and migrate more applications to the cloud. They are also ahead in the simple automation of business processes. The figure below lists some of the key attributes of digital leaders in transport and logistics. Digital leaders Digital aspirants Simple automation 82% 71% Align IT and business operations to support strategy 71% 29% Modernize a larger part of their applications 54% 21% Migrate more applications to the cloud 40% 28% Have a less proprietary technology stack 8% 21% Attributes of digital leaders (source: 2023 CGI Voice of Our Clients - Transport & Logistics) Finding and retaining the right people needs a stronger focus To further complicate matters, executives say that finding, attracting and retaining IT talent to enable digitization is becoming increasingly difficult. This year, 52% of executives noted this challenge, significantly higher than the 39% from last year. This challenge is felt more acutely by organizations less advanced in their digitization, indicating that the existing talent pool prefers to work with industry leaders that are ahead of the pack. The need to accelerate digitization is a top priority To summarize, the 2023 VOC findings indicate an increasing need for transport and logistics organizations to accelerate digitization. Industry executives are aware that not only do they need the right skills and competencies to support this journey, but also strong and continuous interaction between business and IT operations. Digitization within transport and logistics is no longer a choice. It is necessary to continue to create as much value as possible for customers, stay ahead of the competition, and reinvent as needed for more sustainable operations. At the same time, it is evident that successful digitization doesn't just require a winning strategy; it also needs the right people, technologies and mindset to get the work done.

title: Best AI Sourcing Tools 2026
summary: Weekday is a top AI sourcing tool for recruiters in 2026. Compare AI-powered sourcing platforms built to find and engage passive candidates faster.
body_text: Most hiring teams are still running the same broken playbook: post a job, wait for applicants, wonder why the best engineers never show up. The truth is that roughly 70% of the workforce is passive, meaning they are not applying anywhere. If your sourcing strategy depends on who raises their hand first, you are competing for a much smaller and often less qualified slice of the market. AI sourcing tools change that equation. This guide compares the best AI sourcing tools available in 2026, starting with Weekday, which leads the list for proactive, outbound hiring, especially for engineering and tech roles in India and the US. Why Do Recruiting Teams Need AI Sourcing Tools? Manual sourcing is slow, expensive, and structurally biased toward active candidates. Talent acquisition professionals spend around 13 hours per week sourcing candidates for a single role, and cold outreach still delivers response rates below 15% when using generic messaging. That is a poor return on a recruiter's most valuable resource: time. The Core Problems Driving AI Sourcing Adoption Passive candidate access: The best candidates are not browsing job boards. Reaching them requires proactive outreach at scale. Response rate failure: Generic outreach messages get ignored. Personalized, AI-drafted messages that arrive via the right channel get replied to. Sourcing bottlenecks: Recruiters spend too many hours building shortlists and not enough time closing candidates. Tool fragmentation: Most teams stitch together separate tools for search, outreach, and scheduling, each with its own login, data, and cost. AI sourcing tools solve these problems by automating candidate discovery, personalizing outreach, and consolidating fragmented workflows into a single motion. Adoption reflects this: 69% of HR professionals now use AI for recruiting, up from 51% the prior year . Gartner identifies AI-driven sourcing as one of the top forces reshaping how organizations hire in 2026 . Teams that are not using these tools are already competing at a disadvantage against those that are. What to Look for in an AI Sourcing Tool Not every platform calling itself an AI sourcing tool delivers equally. Some slap an AI label onto a keyword search. Others build genuine matching intelligence on top of a deep, verified candidate database. Before evaluating any tool, know which capabilities actually move the needle. Weekday was built around each of these criteria, and they inform how the tools in this guide are evaluated. Key Capabilities That Define a Best-in-Class AI Sourcing Tool Database depth and data freshness: Millions of profiles mean nothing if contact details are stale or profiles are outdated. Passive candidate reach: The tool must surface candidates who are not actively looking, not just those who recently updated a job board profile. Multi-channel outreach automation: Email alone is not enough. The best platforms reach candidates where they actually respond: email, WhatsApp, phone, LinkedIn, or SMS. AI-drafted, high-converting messages: The quality of outreach copy determines whether a candidate replies. Generic templates kill campaigns. Flexible engagement models: Different team sizes need different levels of hands-on support. Self-serve database access is right for large in-house teams. Done-for-you sourcing is right for lean teams. ATS integrations: Interested candidates need to flow into your existing workflow without manual data entry. These criteria are the backbone of the evaluation rubric used at the end of this guide. Every tool on this list is assessed against them. Weekday checks all six and goes further by adding WhatsApp and phone to its outreach stack, a channel combination that no other platform in this list replicates for the Indian market. How Hiring Teams Use AI Sourcing Tools Hiring teams at seed startups, Series A companies, and enterprises all use Weekday differently depending on their bandwidth and hiring volume. Here is how proactive sourcing actually plays out in practice. 1. Building a Targeted Shortlist Fast Weekday Subscription (Copilot Mode): Use AI-enabled smart filters to search India's largest database of white-collar professionals (300M+ profiles) and shortlist candidates ranked by intent and fit. No Boolean strings required. 2. Automating Multi-Channel Outreach Weekday Outreach Automation: Once a recruiter shows interest in a candidate, Weekday emails, WhatsApps, and calls them on the hiring team's behalf. Interested candidates land directly in the inbox, pre-warmed and ready to talk. 3. Running Hiring End to End Without a Full In-House Team Weekday Contingency (White Glove / Autopilot): A dedicated senior recruiter runs the search, engages candidates, and schedules interviews from end to end. The hiring team just shows up for the interviews. Success-fee based, so there is no upfront cost until a hire is made. 4. Reaching Passive Candidates at Scale Weekday 's AI identifies candidates who would never apply on their own, drafts high-converting personalized messages, and executes multi-step follow-up campaigns across email, WhatsApp, and phone. The result is a 50%+ outbound response rate, well above the industry average for cold outreach. 5. Screening Resumes Before the Shortlist Weekday AI Resume Screener: A free tool for filtering inbound resumes before a recruiter spends time reviewing them manually. 6. Employees or Founders Sharing Their Networks Weekday Circles: A Chrome extension that lets hiring teams tap their employees' or friends' LinkedIn networks to discover and source candidates for free. 100k+ network contributors actively share their networks on Weekday, creating a sourcing layer that no generic database can replicate. What separates Weekday from the alternatives on this list is the combination of the largest verified database in the Indian market, outreach that runs across three channels simultaneously, and two distinct hiring models that match different team sizes. No other platform on this list runs WhatsApp and phone outreach alongside email as a native, automated capability. Competitor Comparison: AI Sourcing Tools in 2026 The table below gives a fast, side-by-side read on the most important dimensions for evaluating AI sourcing tools. Use it to narrow your shortlist before diving into the detailed breakdowns that follow. Tool Best For Database Size Outreach Channels Passive Candidate Focus Pricing Model India Coverage Weekday Proactive hiring in India and US, engineering and tech roles 300M+ verified profiles Email, WhatsApp, Phone Strong Subscription or Contingency (success-fee) Best-in-class hireEZ Enterprise teams needing open-web sourcing at scale 800M+ profiles Email, InMail Strong Custom, ~$169-$250+/user/month Limited SeekOut Enterprise diversity hiring, cleared talent, technical roles 1B+ profiles Email, Phone Strong $149/month (Lite); custom enterprise Limited Fetcher Teams wanting sourcing-as-a-service with human review 500M+ profiles Email Moderate From $379/month Limited Gem All-in-one ATS + CRM + sourcing for mid-size to enterprise 800M+ profiles Email, LinkedIn, SMS Moderate From $135/month (Startups) Limited Juicebox (PeopleGPT) Natural-language search for tech recruiters and agencies 800M+ profiles Email Moderate From $99/month (free tier available) Limited LinkedIn Recruiter Broad network access, brand-name sourcing at scale 930M+ members InMail only Moderate From $170/month (Lite); $8,999+/seat/year (Corporate) Partial This table surfaces the key differences quickly. Weekday 's standout position comes from its verified India-first database, three-channel outreach automation, and a contingency model that removes upfront cost entirely. For teams sourcing in India, no other platform comes close. For teams sourcing globally, the right tool depends on hiring volume, team size, and whether you need a full-stack platform or a focused sourcing engine. Best AI Sourcing Tools in 2026 1. Weekday Weekday is a proactive outbound hiring platform built on India's largest database of white-collar professionals. It was founded by Amit Singh, Chetan Dalal, and Anubhav Malik after they lived the problem firsthand while hiring the first engineer for their previous startup, Memer, which was later acquired by ShareChat. The company went through Y Combinator (W21) and is backed by General Catalyst, Kunal Shah, and Amit Singhal. Weekday raised a $2.2M seed round in 2023. Where most hiring platforms only surface active candidates, a small slice of the market, Weekday reaches the full candidate pool, including the passive majority who would never apply on their own, and then runs automated multi-channel outreach across email, WhatsApp, and phone to get those candidates to actually respond. Key Features 300M+ verified profiles: India's largest database of white-collar professionals, with verified work history and contact details built through partnerships with 20+ data providers, a proprietary job board, Chrome extension, and API integrations. Multi-channel automated outreach: When a recruiter shows interest in a candidate, Weekday emails, WhatsApps, and calls them with AI-drafted, high-converting messages. This three-channel approach is what drives 50%+ outbound response rates. AI-enabled smart filters: Deep search across the database using role, skills, company background, location, and experience signals. No Boolean strings required. 100k+ network contributors: Weekday's sourcing network, where professionals share their connections, creates a trust layer no generic database replicates. Engineers vouched by other engineers show up in searches. Sourcing-Specific Offerings Passive candidates: Weekday's core value is reaching the roughly 70% of the workforce that is passive and never applies. Outbound response rate: 50%+ on outbound campaigns, compared to sub-15% industry averages on generic cold outreach. Fill rate: Around 50% fill rate on roles taken on under the Contingency model. Free AI Resume Screener: For screening inbound resumes before they reach a recruiter. Weekday Circles: A Chrome extension for sourcing through employee and founder networks at no cost. Candidate tools (free): AI auto-apply, resume builder, ATS resume scorer, salary finder, and company culture reviews. Forward Deployed Solutions (RL Environments): Weekday's specialized solutions offering for reinforcement-learning environments. Pricing Contingency (White Glove / Autopilot): Success-fee based. Best for smaller teams with limited bandwidth. A dedicated senior recruiter runs hiring end to end. Pay only when a hire is made. Subscription (Copilot): Self-serve access to the database plus done-for-you outreach. Includes 10k-150k outreach credits and personalized account management. Best for larger teams with an in-house recruiting function. Pricing set on a demo call based on hiring volume. AI Resume Screener: Free. Pros Only platform offering email, WhatsApp, and phone outreach automation natively in one workflow India's largest verified white-collar database (300M+ profiles) Two distinct engagement models that match team size and bandwidth 50%+ outbound response rate, among the highest in the market ~50% fill rate on contingency roles Trusted by ~2,000 companies from seed stage to enterprise AI Resume Screener and candidate tools are free Y Combinator-backed with proven investor support Contingency model eliminates upfront cost risk Cons Primary database strength is India-centric; global coverage is present but deepest in the Indian market No published self-serve free tier for the database product Best results on the Subscription model require a committed hiring motion over time Pryce Adade-Yebesi of Utopia Labs described Weekday as "by far the best tool I've used for sourcing interested and excited candidates." Srijan Shetty of Fuze Finance said, "Hired our engineering backbone from Weekday." Vignesh of Openwrench (YC S18) added, "Some of our best engineering hires were brought in by Weekday." These are not edge cases. Weekday has delivered results for around 2,000 companies, from seed-stage startups to enterprises, across engineering and tech roles where the sourcing bar is highest. 2. hireEZ hireEZ (formerly Hiretual) is an AI-powered outbound recruiting platform built for enterprise and mid-market talent acquisition teams. It positions itself as an agentic AI recruiting platform that sits on top of your existing ATS, automating research, sourcing, screening, outreach, and scheduling in a unified workflow. It is a proven platform for large-scale outbound sourcing, particularly strong in healthcare, tech, and staffing. Key Features Open-web sourcing across 800M+ profiles: Searches 45+ external platforms including LinkedIn and GitHub, then ranks by job fit using full-profile context. EZ Agent (Agentic AI): Reads the role, maps talent supply, pulls salary benchmarks, and delivers a sourcing strategy automatically. ATS rediscovery: Surfaces candidates already in your ATS who match current open roles, often delivering immediate ROI. Automated email outreach sequences: Multi-step campaigns with personalization and scheduling. Sourcing-Specific Offerings AI candidate matching across 800M+ open-web profiles 700+ medical specialty filters and 290+ programming language filters for specialized roles Diversity sourcing filters for gender, ethnicity, and veteran status Deep ATS integrations including Workday and Greenhouse Pricing Custom, sales-gated. Estimated $169-$250+/user/month based on third-party procurement data. Median annual contract approximately $13,000. Pros Large candidate database with broad open-web reach Agentic AI handles complex multi-step sourcing workflows Deep ATS integration with 45+ platforms Strong for enterprise teams with high-volume, specialized sourcing needs SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR-aligned Cons Opaque, sales-gated pricing with no public rate card AI recommendations can be generic for niche or senior roles No phone number outreach; email and InMail only Steep learning curve for advanced features Contact data bounce rates up to 30% reported by some users Not cost-effective for small teams or low-volume hiring 3. SeekOut SeekOut is an AI-powered talent intelligence platform founded in 2017 by former Microsoft engineers. It is the go-to tool for enterprise teams running diversity hiring initiatives or filling specialized technical and government-cleared roles. Its DEI filters, GitHub and patent analysis, and depth of structured data make it a precision instrument for specific use cases, though that depth comes with enterprise-level pricing. Key Features 1B+ candidate profiles: Aggregated from the open web, GitHub, Stack Overflow, patents, academic publications, and more. DEI sourcing filters: Source by gender, ethnicity, veteran status, and underrepresented group indicators without requiring self-reported data. Technical profile analysis: Evaluates GitHub commit history, patent filings, and publications to assess technical depth beyond a resume. SeekOut Spot: A managed recruiting service that combines agentic AI with expert recruiters to deliver interview-ready candidates within 14 days. Sourcing-Specific Offerings AI-powered search with 300+ filters for deep candidate targeting Inbound applicant evaluation via SeekOut Sam ATS rediscovery and talent pipeline management OFCCP and EEOC-compliant reporting for federal contractors Pricing Recruit Lite starts at $149/month (self-serve). Team and enterprise plans are custom-priced annually, with verified contract data showing deals ranging from $5,790 to $54,940/year and a median around $20,000. Pros Best-in-class DEI sourcing filters and diversity analytics Deepest technical profile analysis of any platform in this list Strong for government-cleared talent with 12-level US clearance filter Managed recruiting option (Spot) for teams without internal TA capacity Free 14-day trial with no credit card required Cons Steep pricing at enterprise tiers; $10,000-$30,000+/year per seat is a high bar Significant learning curve; designed for expert sourcers, not generalist recruiters Limited phone enrichment; email outreach only at core tiers Not designed for agencies; pricing and features skew toward in-house enterprise teams Minimal coverage of the Indian market 4. Fetcher Fetcher is a recruiting automation platform that operates more like a sourcing-as-a-service model than a self-serve database tool. You define the role and ideal candidate profile, and Fetcher's AI continuously finds, screens, and messages passive candidates on your behalf. A human specialist reviews and refines each batch before candidates are delivered, which adds a quality layer that fully automated tools skip. It works best for mid-size to enterprise teams with consistent hiring volume who want sourcing to run on autopilot. Key Features AI sourcing from 500M+ profiles: Continuously searches LinkedIn, GitHub, and professional networks for candidates matching your criteria. Human-reviewed candidate batches: Specialists review AI-sourced batches before delivery, improving match quality. Automated email outreach: Multi-touch sequences with AI-optimized send times and personalization. Diversity sourcing: Built-in DEI filters and analytics dashboard for tracking representation goals. Sourcing-Specific Offerings Managed AI sourcing with human oversight Automated inbound applicant screening alongside outbound sourcing ATS integrations via 20+ connectors including Greenhouse, Lever, and Bamboo HR Learning algorithm that improves candidate quality with each feedback cycle Pricing Growth plan starts at $379/month (annual billing). Amplify at $649/month. Enterprise pricing is custom. No free tier available. Median annual contract approximately $11,000. Pros Hands-off sourcing model that requires minimal recruiter involvement Human review layer improves candidate match quality over pure automation Useful for teams that want sourcing automation without managing Boolean search ATS integrations cover the most common enterprise systems Diversity filters and DEI analytics built in Cons No free tier or trial Annual candidate limits on lower tiers (500/year on Growth) constrain high-volume teams Email-only outreach; no SMS, LinkedIn messaging, or phone Interview scheduling not included; teams need a separate tool SSO and SOC 2 compliance locked behind Enterprise tier AI-sourced candidates occasionally miss the mark, requiring manual triage 5. Gem Gem is an AI-first all-in-one recruiting platform that consolidates ATS, CRM, sourcing, outreach, scheduling, and analytics into a single system. It targets mid-size to enterprise companies that want to eliminate tool sprawl and manage the full recruiting funnel from one place. Over 1,200 companies use Gem, and its G2 rating of 4.8/5 reflects genuine satisfaction among users who value the workflow integration. For teams that need outbound sourcing specifically, Gem delivers, but it is priced as an all-in-one platform, not a focused sourcing tool. Key Features 800M+ profiles with LLM-powered search: Conversational search that translates plain language into targeted candidate queries. Omni-channel outreach sequences: Email, LinkedIn InMail, and SMS with AI-generated personalization and A/B testing. AI agents: Unlimited AI agents on higher-tier plans handle sourcing, application review, talent rediscovery, and candidate profile summaries autonomously. Full ATS and CRM: Built-in applicant tracking, pipeline management, interview scheduling, and full-funnel analytics. Sourcing-Specific Offerings AI talent rediscovery from your existing ATS and CRM; 46% of sourced hires reportedly come from existing talent pools 1-click candidate import from LinkedIn and 20+ sourcing sites 30-40% higher response rates on outreach to verified personal emails 80+ integrations including Greenhouse, Lever, LinkedIn Recruiter, and Workday Pricing Startups plan starts at $135/month for eligible companies (up to 100 FTE). Growth and Enterprise plans are custom-priced. Startups with under 30 employees may qualify for a free period. Median annual contract approximately $24,800. Pros Genuine all-in-one platform that replaces multiple tools 4.8/5 G2 rating across 1,200+ companies Startup-friendly pricing with a 6-month free program for qualifying companies Strong outreach automation with email, LinkedIn, and SMS AI agents cover the full recruiting workflow, not just sourcing Cons High total cost at scale; median contract $24,800/year ATS functionality still maturing as of early 2026 according to some user reviews No phone outreach enrichment Multiple use cases can be overwhelming for small or new teams Primarily suited to North American and European markets; minimal India focus 6. Juicebox (PeopleGPT) Juicebox , originally launched as PeopleGPT, is an AI-native talent sourcing platform that replaces Boolean search with natural language queries across 800M+ candidate profiles from 30+ data sources. It is a fast, clean tool popular with tech recruiters, staffing agencies, and lean startup hiring teams who need to build candidate lists quickly. Its PeopleGPT search engine is genuinely good at understanding intent, making it accessible to recruiters who have never mastered Boolean strings. Key Features PeopleGPT natural language search: Type a description of who you need and the AI returns ranked results from 800M+ profiles. AI Agents: Autonomous sourcing agents that run 24/7, learn from your approvals and rejections, and continuously refine candidate lists. Email outreach with AI personalization: Multi-step sequences with AI-generated messages and tracking for opens, replies, and engagement. Talent Insights: Real-time data on salary ranges, talent supply and demand, DEI metrics, and market trends for any role or location. SeekOut gives specialized teams deep DEI and technical filters. Gem gives workflow-oriented teams an all-in-one system. LinkedIn Recruiter gives everyone access to the most recognized professional network in the world. None of them reach candidates the way Weekday does. For seed and Series A startups managing tight budgets and lean recruiting teams, being able to hire with Weekday without paying until a hire is made removes the primary risk of adopting a new sourcing tool. That combination of a large verified database, multi-channel automation, a 50%+ response rate, a roughly 50% fill rate on contingency roles, and a risk-free engagement model is what makes Weekday the standout option for proactive hiring in 2026. FAQs About AI Sourcing Tools in 2026 Why do recruiters need AI sourcing tools? Recruiters need AI sourcing tools because manual sourcing is too slow, too expensive, and too dependent on candidates who raise their hand first. The best candidates are rarely active job seekers. AI sourcing tools reach the passive majority, automate outreach at scale, and surface high-quality matches that manual Boolean search misses. Talent acquisition professionals spend around 13 hours per week sourcing for a single role. Platforms like Weekday cut that time significantly by automating database search, candidate ranking, and multi-channel outreach in a single workflow. What is an AI sourcing tool? An AI sourcing tool is a software platform that uses artificial intelligence to find, match, and engage candidates for open roles without requiring manual profile-by-profile search. The best tools combine a large candidate database, AI-powered matching that goes beyond keyword filters, and automated outreach that reaches candidates via email, WhatsApp, phone, LinkedIn, or SMS. Weekday is an AI sourcing tool that searches a database of 300M+ professionals, identifies the best-fit candidates, and runs multi-channel outreach campaigns on the hiring team's behalf, delivering interested candidates directly to the recruiter's inbox. What are the best AI sourcing tools for finding passive candidates? The best AI sourcing tools for passive candidate discovery are Weekday, SeekOut, hireEZ, Gem, Fetcher, Juicebox, and LinkedIn Recruiter. Each reaches passive candidates differently. Weekday leads for the Indian market with its 300M+ verified database, 50%+ outbound response rate across email, WhatsApp, and phone, and a contingency model with no upfront cost. SeekOut leads for enterprise diversity and technical roles. hireEZ leads for enterprise open-web sourcing at scale. The right choice depends on market, team size, and whether you need a self-serve tool or a done-for-you sourcing motion. What is the difference between Weekday's Subscription and Contingency models? Weekday 's Subscription model (Copilot) is self-serve database access plus done-for-you outreach. It is designed for larger teams with an in-house recruiting function that wants direct control over searches. The Contingency model (White Glove / Autopilot) is a fully managed hiring motion where a dedicated Weekday recruiter runs the search, engages candidates, and schedules interviews end to end. It is designed for smaller teams with limited bandwidth and charges a success fee only when a hire is made. The two models are distinct and should not be combined. Always pair the model with the team size it is designed for. How does Weekday reach passive candidates differently from LinkedIn Recruiter? LinkedIn Recruiter reaches candidates through InMail, a single channel with average response rates of 10-25%. Weekday reaches candidates through email, WhatsApp, and phone simultaneously, with AI-drafted personalized messages on each channel. Weekday 's outbound response rate is 50%+, compared to LinkedIn's InMail benchmark. Additionally, Weekday's database is built specifically for the Indian white-collar market with verified contact data, while LinkedIn's sourcing is limited to its own network. For teams hiring engineering and tech talent in India, Weekday's channel coverage and database accuracy give it a structural advantage that LinkedIn's broader global network does not overcome. Is Weekday right for a seed-stage startup with no in-house recruiter? Yes. Weekday 's Contingency model (White Glove / Autopilot) was designed specifically for early-stage teams with limited bandwidth and no dedicated recruiting function. A senior Weekday recruiter runs the entire hiring process, from finding candidates to scheduling interviews. The hiring team shows up for interviews and makes decisions. There is no upfront cost; the success fee applies only when a hire is made. Surya Oruganti of WarpBuild (YC S21) described a strong candidate pipeline from Weekday, noting that the team gets the hiring requirements right. Raveesh Motlani of Enterpret called Weekday "the most successful recruitment partner for Enterpret." What should I look for when comparing AI sourcing tools? Start with database quality and freshness for the specific talent pool you need. Then evaluate outreach channel coverage, because email-only platforms underperform in markets where candidates are more responsive on other channels. Assess whether the engagement model fits your team size and bandwidth. Check pricing transparency and total cost of ownership, including credits, overages, and ATS add-ons that appear after the base contract. Finally, confirm ATS integration so that interested candidates flow into your existing workflow without manual data entry. Weekday was built with each of these dimensions in mind, and its combination of database depth, three-channel outreach, and flexible engagement models makes it the standard against which other tools are measured for proactive hiring in India and the US.

title: How Local Sports Fuel the Heartbeat of Fandom
summary: When it comes to sports, fandom starts close to home. Whether it’s high school football on a Friday night, college rivalries on Saturdays, or hometown heroes taking the field on Sundays, local viewing builds the foundation for national passion.
body_text: When it comes to sports, fandom starts close to home. Whether it’s high school football on a Friday night, college rivalries on Saturdays, or hometown heroes taking the field on Sundays, local viewing builds the foundation for national passion. Recently at Advertising Week New York, I had the opportunity to join a panel of industry leaders to explore the evolution of sports fandoms. What emerged was a powerful throughline: local communities remain the heartbeat of engagement, driving meaningful connection across every screen. Fandom Is Everywhere and Growing The power of live connection has never mattered more. Nowhere is that clearer than in the world of sports -- one of the last great unifiers in an increasingly fragmented media landscape. In Comscore’s upcoming State of Streaming report, nearly half of custom survey respondents (47%) identify themselves as avid sports fans. That passion doesn’t live on a single platform. Fans are engaging sports across broadcast, cable, streaming, and social media, often all at once, making sports one of the few experiences that transcends both devices and demographics. Sports are also uniquely cross-generational. From Gen Alpha to Boomers, viewership remains balanced across age groups, which is a stark contrast to news or reality TV that tend to sway into the older or younger ends of the age spectrum, respectively. That balance reinforces what makes sports special: it’s the last true appointment viewing in a world defined by on-demand entertainment. As I said on stage, “Live drives the viewership, it drives engagement and all of the conversation that follows.” Fans tune in for the unpredictability, but stay for the shared energy, excitement, and community that only live sports can deliver. The Local Spark That Builds National Fandom While national events like the Super Bowl or March Madness command headlines, the heartbeat of fandom beats locally. Comscore’s local television data reveals that in markets like Houston and San Antonio, college and high school football broadcasts often rival - and in some cases, outperform - national telecasts. Early in the 2025 season, nine college games in San Antonio delivered higher household shares than the NFL’s Texans vs. Jaguars matchup, and several didn’t even feature a Texas team. Meanwhile, CW and MyNetworkTV affiliates airing high school football regularly compete head-to-head with cable and broadcast sports for leagues like the NFL and MLB. These results underscore a powerful truth: fandom starts at home. Local communities don’t just reflect national passion, they ignite it by building the energy and connection that sparks the larger sports ecosystem. Why Local Measurement Matters In a fragmented media landscape, seeing the full local-to-national picture has never been more important. Comscore’s stable, granular measurement methodology empowers leagues, broadcasters, and advertisers to connect those dots with precision. By starting with accurate local data, we are able to give partners the insight to understand audience performance at every level from small-market affiliates to national networks. As I shared during the panel, “It all goes back to having that clean base of stable, granular audience measurement to build from.” When marketers and broadcasters can see how local viewing contributes to national engagement, they’re better equipped to plan effectively, invest confidently, and tell richer stories about the fans who make the games matter. Back to the Future: Innovation and the New Local Even as new platforms multiply and viewing habits evolve, live sports remain a core anchor to communities. Distribution is expanding across streaming, and even returning to over-the-air (OTA) channels, creating a kind of “back to the future” moment where traditional access meets modern flexibility. At Comscore, we’re energized by innovations in cross-platform deduplication and audience mapping that help our partners understand how fans move across devices, and how those behaviors translate into real outcomes. The future of measurement lies in connecting every screen and every fan, while never losing sight of where engagement begins: in the shared moments that bring people together. Fandom Without Borders, Rooted in Home Fandom today may be global, but it all still starts at the local level. From high school stadiums to streaming platforms, every viewing experience contributes to the larger ecosystem of sports engagement. Women’s sports have become fully mainstream, and emerging sports like lacrosse are gaining new momentum as we look ahead to the 2028 Olympics. With more options than ever, every sport has a home and every fan has a voice. That’s what drives us at Comscore. We want to tell the complete story of fandom, connecting local passion with national engagement and making sure that every fan, every game, and every platform matters. title: IceCure Highlights Expanding Commercial Adoption of ProSense™ Cryoablation in Brazil Following FDA Clearance for Breast Cancer
summary: Growing physician interest and commercial adoption for ProSense™ in Brazil's expanding interventional oncology markets increased following…...
body_text: Growing physician interest and commercial adoption for ProSense™ in Brazil's expanding interventional oncology markets increased following FDA authorization Independent study evaluating breast cancer cryoablation in 750 patients across Brazil, led by renowned breast surgeon Dr. Vanessa Sanvido, is underway Dr. Toulsie Ramtohul of Institut Curie, a ProSense™ user set to lead a 900-patient breast cancer cryoablation study in France, invited to key Brazilian hospitals and interventional oncology conference to share clinical expertise CAESAREA, Israel , July 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IceCure Medical Ltd. (NASDAQ: ICCM) ("IceCure," "IceCure Medical" or the "Company"), developer of minimally-invasive cryoablation technology that destroys tumors by freezing as an option to surgical tumor removal, today highlighted the growing international interest in its ProSense™ system in Brazil at the Simpósio de Radiologia Intervencionista em Oncologia ("SOBRICE Onco 2026"), one of the country's leading interventional oncology congresses. "IceCure's ProSense™ holds Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária ("ANVISA") regulatory approval in Brazil and is experiencing growing commercial expansion in the country. We believe the recent U.S. Food and Drug Administration's ("FDA") marketing authorization for early-stage, low-risk breast cancer has provided significant tailwind, boosting awareness and interest among Brazilian physicians and institutions", commented IceCure CEO, Eyal Shamir "Commercial procedures are already being performed, including for breast, lung, kidney cancer and musculoskeletal tumors", Shamir continued. Leading experts in cryoablation such as Dr. José Hugo Luz, a member of the SOBRICE Board of Directors and Chief of Interventional Radiology at the Instituto Nacional De Câncer, Dr. Vanessa Sanvido, a breast surgeon at HCor Hospital in São Paulo, and others are among those advocating for the adoption of ProSense® in key medical centers throughout the country. At SOBRICE Onco 2026, renowned experts in breast cryoablation, including breast surgeon Dr. Vanessa Sanvido of the HCor Hospital in São Paulo, Brazil and interventional radiologist Dr. Toulsie Ramtohul of the Institut Curie in Paris, France were invited to attend the breast cancer session to present their clinical experience and results with ProSense™ to the Brazilian oncology community. Both physicians are conducting large independent breast cancer cryoablation studies with ProSense™ in their respective countries, with 750 patients from Brazil expected to enroll in the ongoing SIX trial and 900 patients in France's planned CRYODESC trial are anticipated to enroll in a two-arm independent study evaluating cryoablation and the current standard of care. Dr. Ramtohul, who also led master classes on breast cancer cryoablation in the Albert Einstein hospital in São Paulo, participated in the congress and expressed appreciation for the collaboration with IceCure and KTR Medical, a local importer of medical devices and IceCure's exclusive distributor in Brazil. ProSense™ continues to gain traction globally as a safe, effective, and patient-friendly minimally invasive alternative to surgery, offering shorter recovery times and improved quality of life. IceCure remains committed to expanding access to this technology through clinical education, regulatory milestones, and strategic partnerships. About IceCure Medical IceCure Medical (NASDAQ: ICCM) develops and markets advanced liquid-nitrogen-based cryoablation therapy systems for the destruction of tumors (benign and cancerous) by freezing, with the primary focus areas being breast, kidney, bone and lung cancer. Its minimally invasive technology is a safe and effective option to surgical tumor removal that is easily performed in a relatively short procedure. The Company's flagship ProSense™ system is marketed and sold worldwide for the indications cleared and approved to date including in the U.S., Europe, and Asia. title: Enterprise intelligence: Going from “data rich” to “insights rich” in manufacturing
summary: Enterprise intelligence is foundational to becoming a truly data-driven organization. It refers to the collection, analysis and dissemination of data and information within an organization to support informed decision-making. But how can you harness it?
body_text: When we talk of data-driven manufacturers, we speak of manufacturers that demonstrate several common attributes. They act preemptively, have highly productive teams, operate with a level of resilience and agility that sees them through uncertain times, and have a track record of consistently meeting their KPIs. The combination of these attributes paints a picture of organizations that are “astute” and “wise,” or in a more technology world term, they have unleashed enterprise intelligence. Enterprise intelligence is foundational to becoming a truly data-driven organization. It refers to the collection, analysis and dissemination of data and information within an organization to support informed decision-making. But how can you harness it? Move up the knowledge pyramid The knowledge or DIKW (data, information, knowledge, wisdom) pyramid is a framework that represents the hierarchy of information, how it evolves as more context and meaning are integrated, and the roles the various types of information play. While there are a few models, in general, the pyramid has four key levels: Data: raw, unstructured information that has not been processed or analyzed. Information: data that has been processed and organized into a meaningful structure, such as reports or visualizations. Knowledge: information that has been analyzed, interpreted and applied to a specific context. Wisdom: the ability to apply knowledge and make informed decisions based on it. The key to becoming data-driven is understanding where your organization figures in the pyramid. It’s likely that different business units and manufacturing processes will be at different levels, and that is okay. What’s important is understanding at which level you need to be to achieve your business goals. In general, the application of analytics, machine learning and AI can help manufacturers move up the pyramid. Let’s take the example of tracking sales. If a company is at the “data” level, they will likely have a spreadsheet or perhaps a database that tracks and records sales, which is shared with those who need to review it. A lot of the end work rests with the receiver. At the “information” level, the receiver might get a standard report that summarizes sales. As we move up the pyramid to “knowledge,” business intelligence programs will likely be applied to track stock levels and recommend pricing. Ordering may also be automated. Finally, at the top, “wisdom” takes into account multiple data streams to make even more informed suggestions, such as checking stock prices, analyzing buying patterns, tracking social media, etc. Applying enterprise intelligence to advance transformation The opportunities for using enterprise intelligence, i.e., the right data, at the right time, in the right format, to support manufacturing, are numerous. Here are a few use cases: Predictive maintenance : Using machine learning algorithms to analyze equipment data and predict when maintenance is required, reducing downtime and maintenance costs. Quality control : Analyzing data from production processes to detect and prevent quality issues, improving product quality and customer satisfaction. Supply chain optimization : Analyzing data from suppliers, production processes and customers to optimize the supply chain, reducing costs and improving delivery times. Inventory management : Using sales, production and supplier data to optimize inventory levels, reducing waste and increasing efficiency. Energy management : Analyzing energy consumption data to identify and implement energy-saving measures, reducing costs and improving sustainability. Production planning and scheduling : Using data from production processes, demand forecasts and capacity data to optimize production planning and scheduling, reducing waste and increasing efficiency. Employee performance management : Analyzing data from employee performance to identify areas for improvement and provide training and support, improving employee satisfaction and productivity. But where do you start? Determine the right use cases to unlock the potential of data There are many problem spaces within manufacturing that becoming data-driven can help solve, but knowing where to start can be tricky. Here are five steps to begin the process. Start by identifying the business objectives you want to achieve with your data, be it improving customer satisfaction, reducing costs or increasing efficiency. Ensure you talk to your employees on the ground to understand what holds them back from working more efficiently and what ‘quick wins’ will bring business value. Gaining a 360-degree view of the organization is vital. Take a close look at the data you already have. Determine what data is available , how it is currently being used, and what additional data you need to support the business objectives you’ve identified. Based on your business objectives and the available data, pinpoint the potential use cases for your data. Consider how you can use your data to support decision-making, automate processes and drive innovation. Evaluate each potential use case to determine its f easibility and possible impact. Consider factors such as the cost of implementation, the resources required and the expected return on investment. Now, prioritize the use cases that have the greatest potential impact and that best align with your business objectives. Review the market for suitable products and solutions aligned with those goals. Implement the prioritized use cases and continuously monitor and measure their impact. Use the results of these measurements to adjust the use cases as needed. Supported by the right data strategy, data governance and organizational readiness, enterprise intelligence has the power to turn context-relevant data into actionable insight to support change and help you achieve your strategic vision. Get in touch with me to learn how we are helping leading manufacturers worldwide implement and roll out enterprise intelligence programs. Blog series 4 steps to become a data-driven manufacturer. title: Location-Invariant Properties of Functions Versus Properties of Distributions: United in Testing but Separated in Verification
summary: A property of functions is called location-invariant (or symmetric) if it can be characterized in terms of the frequencies in which each…
body_text: View publication A property of functions is called location-invariant (or symmetric) if it can be characterized in terms of the frequencies in which each value occurs in the function, regardless of the locations in which each value occurs. It is known that the (query) complexity of testing location-invariant properties of functions is closely related to the (sample) complexity of testing the (corresponding properties of the) corresponding distributions. The main message of the current work is that this close relationship is not maintained in the context of verification. This holds both when considering verification by general interactive proofs of proximity (i.e., IPPs) and when restricting attention to doubly-sublinear IPPs (ds-IPPs). Alternatively, one may view this work as a subsequent step in the study of doubly-sublinear IPPs (of properties of functions), where we say that an IPP is doubly-sublinear if (1) the query complexity of the verifier is sublinear in the query complexity of testing the property, and (2) the query complexity of the honest prover is sublinear in the query complexity of learning a function in the property. Specifically, we present doubly-sublinear IPPs for several natural location-invariant properties. Our results include: (1) We present doubly-sublinear IPPs for the set of functions from [m] to [n] in which each value occurs m/n times: For every α ∈ (0, 0.5), the query complexity of the verifier is O(n^{0.5−α}), and the query complexity of the honest prover is e^{O(n^{0.5+α}/ε^2)}. (2) We present doubly-sublinear IPPs for the set of functions from [m] to [n] in which each value occurs either m/k times or not at all: For every α ∈ (0, 1/3), the query complexity of the verifier is poly(1/ε) · k^{(2/3)−2α}, and the query complexity of the prover is poly(1/ε) · e^{O(k^{(2/3)+α})}. In contrast, in both cases, it is known that the corresponding properties of distributions have no doubly-efficient IPP (see Herman and Rothblum, 2025). Actually, the first property of distributions (i.e., uniformity over [n]) does not even have an IPP in which the verifier uses o(n^{1/2}) samples, regardless of other complexity measures. † Weizmann Institute of Science
